stage.title: Implement async setup, compile, record, and submit orchestration

goal: Enable asynchronous RenderGraph setup and compile, parallel AddPass execution-lambda command recording, and RHIExecutor-backed translate graph submission so frame work can use multi-threaded record plus multi-threaded translate without a second submission model.
entry_gate: The barrier and queue synchronization checkpoint is implemented.
The resource reuse checkpoint compiles lifetimes before record.
RHIExecutor remains the only submit and translate pipeline entrypoint.

hard_rules.rule: AddSetupPass may run graph-owned preparation work before Compile only. Resource access is declared by graph-owned pass parameters and parsed after setup. AddSetupPass must not create RHI resources, update bindless arrays, record commands, or call RHIExecutor.
Worker-thread AddPass execution lambdas record into assigned RHICommandList instances only. They must not submit, present, sync, or mutate global RHI state.
Compiled submit ordering must be explicit before command recording starts. Do not infer submit dependencies after worker lambdas finish.
Do not introduce a RenderGraph-owned GPU submission backend. Submit through RHIExecutor.
Do not let record workers allocate pass parameters or compiled resource tables from transient thread-local storage unless ownership is transferred into the RG allocator before Compile freezes.
Do not emit unmatched GPU scope begin/end events into separate CommandLists without a compiled scope id and explicit ordering relation.
Do not add a second AddPass setup callback during async record implementation. Setup work stays in AddSetupPass.
Do not let execution lambdas declare graph-level GPU scopes. RG_EVENT_SCOPE declarations are compiled before record starts.
Do not let RenderGraph record workers access backend platform command-list handles. Worker threads record abstract RHICommandList commands only.

checkpoints.title: Implement AddSetupPass contract
checkpoints.problem: Graph construction can run in parallel only if setup code is pure declaration work and cannot touch live RHI submission state.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: AddSetupPass tasks prepare graph-owned CPU data before Compile and do not declare resource access.
Setup output is immutable input to Compile.
Invalid setup behavior is rejected by API shape or debug assertions.
Setup does not depend on RHI command list lifetime, and compile reads resource access from pass parameters after setup has finished.

checkpoints.title: Implement asynchronous Compile
checkpoints.problem: Barrier, lifetime, queue, and submit planning should be compiled before record and can use task parallelism once setup output is immutable.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Compile runs dependency analysis, culling, lifetime assignment, barrier batching, queue segmentation, and submit-plan generation.
Compile output is immutable and can be consumed by record tasks without locks around graph mutation.
Compile produces clear failure diagnostics for unknown first read, undeclared bindless access, unsupported pool reuse, and multi-source queue segment violations.
Compile can run synchronously for simple callers and asynchronously for frame pipelines without changing semantics.

checkpoints.title: Implement parallel AddPass execution-lambda recording
checkpoints.problem: Pass command recording should scale across worker threads, but each lambda needs a stable resolved view set and a command list with no shared mutable command stream.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Compile assigns record groups by queue, pass ordering layer, and dependency compatibility.
Each record task receives one RHICommandList, graph-owned parameters, and a read-only resolved resource table.
Record tasks may run in parallel when compiled hazards and queue order allow it.
RHICommandList ownership is single-writer and returned to the graph only after the task completes.
Record tasks never receive backend platform command-list handles; platform external work is represented as typed RHI commands for backend translate.
AddPass still has exactly one execution lambda; preparation data comes from AddSetupPass and resource access comes from graph.Alloc<T>() parameters.

checkpoints.title: Compile RHIExecutor submit and translate graph
checkpoints.problem: Parallel record is not enough; the graph must also submit command lists in a shape that lets RHIExecutor translate in parallel and submit with correct GPU ordering.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RenderGraph emits an ordered submit plan containing CommandLists, queue identity, host translate prerequisites, GPU wait/signal requirements, and present/export tails.
The main thread hands the compiled command-list batch to RHIExecutor::Submit.
RHIExecutor retains ownership of translate tasks, submission runtime, interrupt completion, and Sync semantics.
RenderGraph does not bypass RHIExecutor or duplicate its translate scheduler.

checkpoints.title: Add focused async record and translate validation cases
checkpoints.problem: Async setup, record, and translate bugs require stress cases that prove worker threads never submit and that compiled dependencies survive parallel execution.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Tests cover parallel setup, parallel compile, parallel record, multi-queue submit plans, and multi-threaded translate progression.
Tests assert worker-thread paths do not call RHIExecutor::Submit, Present, or Sync.
Tests run through testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 and broader regression through testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1.

checkpoints.title: Implement RG allocator phase ownership
checkpoints.problem: Async setup, compile, and record need stable ownership for graph data and pass parameters. Without a phase-owned allocator, parallel record can observe stale parameter data or mutate graph structures after compile.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Setup tasks allocate pass declarations, RGResource wrappers, and graph.Alloc<T>() parameter objects from the graph setup allocator.
Compile freezes setup allocator data and writes immutable compiled artifacts into the compile allocator.
Record workers consume compiled artifact views and resolved resource tables without mutating setup data.
Frame teardown releases graph CPU allocations only after all record tasks have completed and RHIExecutor has accepted the produced CommandLists.
Long-lived caches are explicitly separate from frame-local RG allocator memory.

checkpoints.title: Compile GPU trace scopes across CommandLists
checkpoints.problem: A graph-level GPU scope may cover passes that compile into multiple CommandLists or multiple queues. Native command-list begin/end stack semantics are insufficient for that logical scope.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RG_EVENT_SCOPE declarations create trace metadata before Compile, and Compile creates a trace scope plan with stable scope ids, parent ids, names, begin points, end points, and queue/submit ordering requirements.
Pass-local scopes emit ordinary begin/end events inside a single CommandList when possible.
Cross-CommandList scopes emit graph-level begin/end marker events with explicit scope ids and depend on compiled submit order instead of stack pairing.
GPUEventStream can reconstruct logical nesting from scope ids and ordering metadata even when events arrive from different CommandLists.
Compile rejects scope shapes that would imply nested ordering across unordered queue work without a synchronization edge.

stage_exit_gate: RenderGraph setup and compile can run asynchronously without RHI side effects.
AddPass execution lambdas record command lists in parallel through single-writer command-list ownership.
The compiled submit plan feeds RHIExecutor and enables multi-threaded translate without a second submission backend.
RG allocator lifetime is phase-owned and GPU trace scopes remain reconstructible across multiple compiled CommandLists.
validation: Run testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 after focused async record and translate tests land.
Run testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after the stage-sized landing.
